title: Sycophancy Probe Replication Across Chat vs. Instruct vs. Base Model Variants

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: understanding whether sycophancy is a pre-training or RLHF artifact directly informs where in the training pipeline to intervene. An RLHF-specific finding would motivate changes to reward modeling.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running the full SAE + linear probe pipeline on both base and instruction-tuned model variants. SAE training is non-trivial. Additionally, base models may not produce sycophantic responses in the standard prompt format, requiring adapted evaluation methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two model variants (base vs. instruct), one pipeline. The core comparison is focused but the prerequisite SAE training work is substantial for a beginner. Still, if limiting to Gemma-2-2B, the models are small.
